definition_zh: 宇宙的；巨大的；至关重要的
definition_en: relating to the cosmos; huge in scale or significance
core_image: X 射线天文望远镜拍到的星系碰撞图，配着人类尺度下的一双手示意大小
scene: 纪录片里解说员说：The collision of two galaxies is a cosmic event that plays out over hundreds of millions of years.
sceneCN: 这里指「宇宙尺度上的」（第1个义项）；句意为两个星系的碰撞是一个在几亿年间展开的 cosmic 事件。

pos.zh: 宇宙的；巨大的；至关重要的

senses.title: Relating to the cosmos or outer space
senses.titleCN: 与宇宙或外太空有关的
senses.definition: the core scientific sense; anything that happens beyond Earth and its atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 核心科学义项：地球和大气层以外发生的任何事
senses.example: Cosmic radiation constantly bombards the upper atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙辐射不断轰击高层大气。
senses.why: cosmic = of the cosmos, just like galactic = of a galaxy.
senses.whyCN: cosmic = 宇宙的，就像 galactic = 星系的。

senses.title: On an immense scale
senses.definition: informal usage: so large or so huge that it dwarfs normal human-scale numbers or events
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法：大到超过人类日常尺度的数字或事件
senses.example: The budget gap was cosmic — billions of dollars over what anyone had projected.
senses.exampleCN: 预算缺口是 cosmic 的——比任何人预期的多几十亿美元。
senses.why: Like astronomical, cosmic can refer to things on the scale of the universe.
senses.whyCN: 和 astronomical 一样，cosmic 可以指宇宙尺度的东西。

senses.title: Cosmic dust, rays, background radiation
senses.titleCN: 宇宙尘、宇宙射线、宇宙背景辐射
senses.definition: scientific compounds: cosmic describes anything in space — dust, rays, noise, microwave background
senses.definitionCN: 科学复合词：cosmic 描述太空里的一切——尘、射线、噪声、微波背景
senses.example: Cosmic microwave background radiation is the echo of the Big Bang.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙微波背景辐射是大爆炸的回声。
senses.why: The adjective is widely attached to nouns in astronomy and astrophysics.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在天文和天体物理里广泛跟名词搭配。

senses.title: Cosmic importance or significance
senses.definition: used for events or decisions that seem as important as anything in the universe
senses.definitionCN: 用于重要得像宇宙里最关键的事件或决定
senses.example: To a child, losing a favourite toy can feel of cosmic importance.
senses.exampleCN: 对小孩来说，丢了最喜欢的玩具可能觉得是 cosmic 级别的事。
senses.why: Hyperbole borrows the largest scale to mean the most important.
senses.whyCN: 夸张借最大的尺度来指最重要的。

senses.title: Cosmic justice or cosmic order
senses.definition: used to describe a moral or natural order that is larger than human society
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述比人类社会更大的道德或自然秩序
senses.example: Some people believe in cosmic justice that balances the wrongs of this life.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人相信 cosmic 正义会平衡这一世的冤屈。
senses.why: Cosmic carries the 'ordered whole' sense from its Greek root kosmos.
senses.whyCN: Cosmic 带着希腊语词根 kosmos 的「有序整体」含义。

senses.title: Cosmic vs astronomical vs galactic
senses.definition: cosmic = whole universe; astronomical = of astronomy or huge; galactic = of galaxies; the scales grow smaller
senses.definitionCN: cosmic = 整个宇宙；astronomical = 天文学的或巨大的；galactic = 星系的；尺度逐个变小
senses.example: Cosmic events span billions of galaxies; galactic events span one galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: Cosmic 事件跨越几十亿星系；galactic 事件只跨一个星系。
senses.why: The progression maps nicely: cosmic > astronomical > galactic.
senses.whyCN: 这个阶梯很清楚：cosmic > astronomical > galactic。

senses.title: Cosmic in popular culture and New Age
senses.titleCN: 流行文化和新世纪运动里的 cosmic
senses.definition: used for anything feeling mystical, universal or out of the ordinary
senses.definitionCN: 用来指神秘的、普遍的或不普通的事物
senses.example: The festival had a cosmic vibe — everyone felt connected to something bigger.
senses.exampleCN: 那个节日有一种 cosmic 的氛围——人人觉得和更伟大的东西连上了。
senses.why: New Age culture picked up cosmic because it evokes vastness, mystery and unity.
senses.whyCN: 新世纪运动喜欢 cosmic 因为它唤起浩瀚、神秘、合一。

senses.title: Cosmic rays and particle physics
senses.definition: high-energy particles from space that hit Earth's atmosphere; studied by particle physicists
senses.definitionCN: 来自太空、轰击地球大气的高能粒子；由粒子物理学家研究
senses.example: Cosmic rays discovered new fundamental particles before accelerators could.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙射线在加速器之前就发现了新的基本粒子。
senses.why: Cosmic rays are nature's own particle accelerator — cheaper and more powerful than anything we can build.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙射线是大自然自己的粒子加速器——比我们能造的都便宜且强大。

intro.cn: cosmic 是 cosmos 的形容词：希腊语 kosmos（有秩序的宇宙）+ -ic 形容词后缀。

items.en: kosmos 'order, ornament, universe' → cosmic via Latin and French.
items.cn: kosmos「秩序、装饰、宇宙」→ 经拉丁语和法语 → cosmic。

items.en: cosmic appeared in English in the early 17th century, borrowed from Latin cosmicus.
items.cn: cosmic 17 世纪早期进入英语，借自拉丁语 cosmicus。

items.en: With the growth of astrophysics in the 20th century, cosmic became attached to dozens of scientific compounds.
items.cn: 20 世纪天体物理成长时，cosmic 与几十个科学复合词搭在一起。

items.en: The 'huge scale' sense developed alongside astronomical and galactic in the 20th century.
items.cn: 「巨大尺度」的义项在 20 世纪和 astronomical, galactic 一起发展起来。

items.en: New Age writers and musicians adopted cosmic in the 1960s and 1970s.
items.cn: 1960-70 年代新世纪作家和音乐人采用 cosmic。

items.en: Scientific, figurative and New Age senses all remain active.
items.cn: 科学、比喻、新世纪的义项今天都活跃。

examples.en: Cosmic dust is one of the key ingredients for forming new stars and planets.
examples.cn: 宇宙尘是形成新恒星和行星的关键成分之一。

examples.en: To a four-year-old, finding their lost teddy bear feels of cosmic importance.
examples.cn: 对四岁小孩来说，找到丢失的泰迪熊感觉是 cosmic 级别的事。

examples.en: The team detected a burst of cosmic rays that could not be explained by known sources.
examples.cn: 团队探测到一次无法用已知来源解释的宇宙射线爆发。

definition_zh: 宇宙；和谐的秩序
definition_en: the universe as an ordered whole; an ordered system
core_image: 星空下一个旋转的星系，配上古代四元素（水、土、气、火）的装饰画
scene: 诗人在诗行里写：From the smallest atom to the farthest galaxy, the cosmos hums with hidden order.
sceneCN: 这里指「整个有秩序的宇宙」（第1个义项）；句意为从最小的原子到最远的星系，宇宙都在隐秘的秩序里嗡嗡作响。

pos.zh: 宇宙；有秩序的整体；（小写 c 时）花簇

senses.title: The universe as an ordered whole
senses.titleCN: 作为有秩序整体的宇宙
senses.definition: the whole of all matter and energy, seen not as chaos but as a system with underlying order and laws
senses.definitionCN: 所有物质和能量的整体，不是混沌的，而是一个有内在秩序和法则的系统
senses.example: Ancient Greek philosophers believed the cosmos was held together by geometric harmony.
senses.exampleCN: 古希腊哲学家相信宇宙由几何和谐维系在一起。
senses.why: kosmos originally meant 'order, arrangement, ornament' before it meant 'the universe'.
senses.whyCN: kosmos 原意是「秩序、安排、装饰」，后来才指「宇宙」。

senses.title: Cosmos flower (lowercase)
senses.definition: a flowering plant of the genus Cosmos, with daisy-like blooms in pink, white or orange
senses.definitionCN: Cosmos 属的开花植物，有粉色、白色或橙色的雏菊状花朵
senses.example: She planted cosmos along the fence and they bloomed all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 她沿围栏种了大波斯菊，整个夏天都在开。
senses.why: The plant was named cosmos because its petals resemble the orderly arrangement of a starburst.
senses.whyCN: 这种花被命名为 cosmos 是因为它的花瓣像星爆的秩序排列。

senses.title: Figurative: any ordered system
senses.titleCN: 比喻：任何有秩序的系统
senses.definition: any interconnected set of things that feels coherent and patterned
senses.definitionCN: 任何相互关联、感觉连贯有模式的事物集
senses.example: Her paintings suggest a cosmos where everything is connected by invisible threads.
senses.exampleCN: 她的画暗示了一个万物被看不见的线连接的有序宇宙。
senses.why: Cosmos carries the sense of ordered system even when scaled down to human size.
senses.whyCN: Cosmos 即使缩小到人类尺度也带着「有秩序系统」的感觉。

senses.title: Universe vs cosmos
senses.definition: universe is the scientific word for everything that exists; cosmos adds the sense of order, harmony and design
senses.definitionCN: universe 是科学词，指一切存在之物；cosmos 增加了秩序、和谐、设计的感觉
senses.example: Cosmologists study the universe, but poets write about the cosmos.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙学家研究 universe，而诗人写 cosmos。
senses.why: The poetic, ordered tone of cosmos comes straight from its Greek root.
senses.whyCN: cosmos 的诗意、有序的语气直接来自它的希腊词根。

senses.title: Microcosm: a small cosmos
senses.definition: a small system that mirrors the larger cosmos; often used for a community or a single person
senses.definitionCN: 反映大宇宙的小系统；常用于社区或单个人
senses.example: The city was a microcosm of the whole country's tensions.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市是整个国家紧张局势的缩影。
senses.why: microcosm uses the same cosmos root to describe a scaled-down version.
senses.whyCN: microcosm 用同一个 cosmos 词根描述缩小的版本。

senses.title: Cosmos in religion and philosophy
senses.definition: used to describe God's creation or a moral order that governs both the heavens and human life
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述上帝的创造或同时支配天上和人间生活的道德秩序
senses.example: The Stoics taught that living in accordance with the cosmos was the highest good.
senses.exampleCN: 斯多葛学派教导说与宇宙和谐一致地生活是最高的善。
senses.why: Cosmos carries ethical weight that universe does not, because it means 'ordered by design'.
senses.whyCN: Cosmos 带有 universe 没有的伦理重量，因为它的意思是「有设计地安排的」。

senses.title: Cosmos in science fiction
senses.definition: used to evoke vastness and wonder, slightly more poetic than universe or galaxy
senses.definitionCN: 用来唤起浩瀚和惊叹，比 universe 或 galaxy 更有诗意
senses.example: The spaceship vanished into the cosmos, never to be seen again.
senses.exampleCN: 飞船消失在宇宙中，再也没出现。
senses.why: Writers reach for cosmos when they want scale to feel beautiful as well as large.
senses.whyCN: 写作者用 cosmos 时想要尺度不仅大还要美。

senses.title: Plural cosmoses
senses.definition: the standard English plural; sometimes used in science fiction for multiple universes
senses.definitionCN: 英语标准复数；科幻里有时指多个宇宙
senses.example: The theory predicts that our cosmos is just one of many cosmoses.
senses.exampleCN: 该理论预言我们的宇宙只是众多宇宙之一。
senses.why: The plural is a natural English adaptation; Greek kosmoi exists but is rarely used in English.
senses.whyCN: 复数是自然的英语形式；希腊语 kosmoi 存在但英语里很少用。

intro.en: cosmos comes from Greek kosmos, which originally meant 'order, arrangement, ornament' before it came to mean 'the ordered universe'.
intro.cn: cosmos 来自希腊语 kosmos，原意是「秩序、安排、装饰」，后来才指「有秩序的宇宙」。

items.en: Homeric Greek kosmos meant 'orderly arrangement, ornament'. By the 5th century BCE it meant 'the world as an ordered whole'.
items.cn: 荷马时代希腊语 kosmos 意为「有序的安排、装饰」。到公元前 5 世纪意为「作为有序整体的世界」。

items.en: Latin borrowed kosmos directly, keeping both the 'order' and 'universe' senses.
items.cn: 拉丁语直接借入 kosmos，保留了「秩序」和「宇宙」两种意思。

items.en: Old French cosmos kept the Greek meaning of 'ordered universe'.
items.cn: 古法语 cosmos 保持希腊语「有秩序的宇宙」含义。

items.en: Middle English cosmos appeared in the 14th century via Old French.
items.cn: 中古英语 cosmos 14 世纪经古法语出现。

items.en: The Cosmos plant genus was named in the 18th century from the Greek word for the universe.
items.cn: Cosmos 属植物在 18 世纪以希腊语宇宙一词命名。

items.en: Poets, philosophers and gardeners use cosmos; scientists prefer universe.
items.cn: 诗人、哲学家、园丁用 cosmos；科学家更常用 universe。

note.en: Group one shares the cosm- root; group two compares cosmos to universe, galaxy and other cosmic terms.
note.cn: 第一组共享 cosm- 词根；第二组把 cosmos 和 universe, galaxy 等宇宙术语对比。

entries.definition: Of or relating to the cosmos.
Study of the origin and structure of the cosmos.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宇宙起源和结构的学科。

entries.definition: Specific study of how the cosmos began.
entries.definitionCN: 专门研究宇宙如何起源。

entries.definition: Scientific word for all that exists; less poetic than cosmos.
entries.definitionCN: 表示一切存在之物的科学词；比 cosmos 少些诗意。

entries.definition: A single system of stars; much smaller than either cosmos or universe.
entries.definitionCN: 一个恒星系统；比 cosmos 和 universe 都小得多。

entries.definition: The underlying sense of cosmos: arrangement, not chaos.
entries.definitionCN: cosmos 的底层含义：有序、非混沌。

entries.definition: The opposite of cosmos in ancient Greek; shapeless, formless matter.
entries.definitionCN: 古希腊语中 cosmos 的对立；无形、无定形之物。

normalIntro.en: Cosmos = ordered universe, not chaos.
normalIntro.cn: Cosmos = 有秩序的宇宙，不是混沌。

normal.en: Greek kosmos meant 'order' before it meant 'universe'.
normal.cn: 希腊语 kosmos 先意为「秩序」，后意为「宇宙」。

normal.en: Cosmos vs chaos: universe with vs without order.
normal.cn: Cosmos vs chaos：有 vs 无秩序的宇宙。

normal.en: Microcosm is a small cosmos, like a city reflecting the country.
normal.cn: Microcosm 是一个小 cosmos，像城市反映国家。

normal.en: The cosmos flower is named for its orderly petals.
normal.cn: 大波斯菊以它有序的花瓣命名为 cosmos。

normal.en: Poets write about the cosmos; scientists about the universe.
normal.cn: 诗人写 cosmos；科学家写 universe。

abstract.en: Ancient Greek philosophers gathering under the stars, listening for harmony.
abstract.cn: 古希腊哲学家聚在星空下，谛听和谐之声。

abstract.en: A single daisy, petals perfectly arranged around a centre.
abstract.cn: 一朵雏菊，花瓣完美地绕中心排列。

abstract.en: Everything connected by invisible threads, humming in tune.
abstract.cn: 万物被看不见的线连着，嗡嗡地共鸣。

examples.en: The Hubble image of the deep cosmos contains over ten thousand galaxies.
examples.cn: 哈勃的深空宇宙图像里包含一万多个星系。

examples.en: According to Stoic philosophy, we should live in harmony with the cosmos.
examples.cn: 按斯多葛哲学，我们应与宇宙和谐生活。

examples.en: She grew cosmos along the garden path where they caught the afternoon sun.
examples.cn: 她在花园小径旁种了大波斯菊，在下午阳光下盛开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 希腊语 kosmos（秩序、装饰）→ 有秩序的宇宙 = cosmos

root: kosmos（希腊语，秩序、装饰）→ cosmos。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses balance the scientific universe, the poetic ordered whole, the flower, figurative systems, microcosm, philosophy, sci-fi and the plural.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项平衡了科学的宇宙、诗意的有序整体、花、比喻系统、小宇宙、哲学、科幻和复数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stars arranged in a galaxy spiral, order out of apparent chaos.
core.cn: 核心意象：星系螺旋里排列的恒星，从看似混沌中显现秩序。

branches.en: THE ORDERED WHOLE: the universe read as order rather than plain extent, which is what separates it from universe.
branches.cn: 有序整体：被读作秩序而非单纯范围的宇宙，这正是它与 universe 的分界。

branches.en: THE FLOWER: the garden genus Cosmos, unrelated to the sky sense.
branches.cn: 花卉：园艺里的波斯菊属，与天空义无关。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE SYSTEMS AND MICROCOSM: any coherent whole, including a small one that mirrors the large.
branches.cn: 比喻系统与小宇宙：任何自洽整体，包括映照大宇宙的小整体。

branches.en: RELIGION, PHILOSOPHY AND SCIENCE FICTION: creation and moral order, then fictional vastness.
branches.cn: 宗教、哲学与科幻：造物与道德秩序，再到虚构的浩瀚。

branches.en: PLURAL FORM: cosmoses, the standard English plural, also used for multiple universes.
branches.cn: 复数形式：cosmoses，英语标准复数，也指多个宇宙。

intro.cn: cosmos 来自希腊语 kosmos「秩序、装饰、宇宙」；cosmo- 前缀在英语科学里多产。

latinIntro.en: kosmos is purely Greek; Latin borrowed it directly without modification.
latinIntro.cn: kosmos 纯希腊语；拉丁语直接借入没改。

definition_zh: v. 宠爱，娇养；悉心照料
definition_en: to treat someone with too much care and attention
core_image: 奶奶把小猫裹进围巾，只露出一张脸
scene: 奶奶把那只小猫捧在怀里，天天宠着。Grandmother cosseted the kitten every single day.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cosset 指宠爱；句意是奶奶天天宠着那只小猫。

senses.title: Pamper
senses.definition: to treat someone with great fondness
senses.definitionCN: 满怀宠爱地对待某人
senses.example: Grandmother cosseted the kitten.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶宠着那只小猫。
senses.why: A kitten wrapped in a scarf.
senses.whyCN: 被围巾裹住的小猫。

senses.title: Protect too much
senses.definition: to shelter someone from every difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 把一切困难挡在外头
senses.example: They cosseted the young player.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把那年轻球员保护得太好。
senses.why: A padded corner round a table.
senses.whyCN: 桌角包着的软垫。

senses.title: Care for tenderly
senses.definition: to look after with great care
senses.definitionCN: 细心照料
senses.example: She cosseted the sick plant.
senses.exampleCN: 她细心养护那株病弱的植物。
senses.why: A plant moved daily to the sun.
senses.whyCN: 每天搬到太阳下的一盆花。

items.en: A cot was a small shelter.
items.cn: cot 意为小棚。

items.en: A cosset was a pet lamb reared by hand.

items.en: English cosset meant a spoiled pet.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 cosset 指娇养的宠物。

items.en: The verb cosset meant to pamper.
items.cn: 十七世纪动词 cosset 意为娇养。

items.en: It now means to overprotect anyone.
items.cn: 现代英语指对任何人过度呵护。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a letter or two; the near-meaning group names over-kind care.
note.cn: 形近组只差一两个字母；近义组都是过分呵护。

definition_zh: 费用；成本；代价；花费
definition_en: the money needed to buy or make something, the loss suffered for a gain, or to have a price
core_image: 一张价签挂在货物上，背后还压着一本看不见的账
scene: 装修报价单摊在桌上，木地板那一项比预期高出一截。The repairs will cost more than we planned.
sceneCN: 这里 cost 指「花费」（第 3 个义项：需要付出某笔钱）；句意是这次维修的花费会超出我们的计划。

senses.title: The money needed
senses.definition: the amount of money that must be paid to buy or make something
senses.definitionCN: 为购买或制造某物必须支付的金额
senses.example: The cost of the ticket surprised us.
senses.exampleCN: 票价让我们吃了一惊。
senses.why: Every object carries an invisible price tag on its back.
senses.whyCN: 每件物品背后都挂着一张看不见的价签。

senses.title: What a gain takes from you
senses.definition: the loss or damage suffered in order to gain something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而承受的损失或损害
senses.example: He won the match at the cost of his health.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢了比赛，代价是健康。
senses.why: Every victory is paid for with something that is not money.
senses.whyCN: 每一场胜利都要用钱以外的东西来支付。

senses.title: To have a price
senses.definition: to have a particular price, or to make someone lose something
senses.definitionCN: 价格为某数，或使某人失去某物
senses.example: The repairs will cost more than we planned.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修的花费会超出我们的计划。
senses.why: The price reaches out from the object and takes money from your hand.
senses.whyCN: 价格从物品那边伸出手，把你手中的钱拿走。

intro.en: Cost comes from Latin constare, to stand firm or stand at a price, through Old French coster, to cost.
intro.cn: cost 来自拉丁语 constare（立定、值某个价钱），经古法语 coster（值…钱）进入英语。

items.en: Constare meant to stand together or stand firm.
items.cn: constare 意为共同站立或稳稳立住。

items.en: The same verb came to mean to stand at a certain price.
items.cn: 同一个动词后来表示标价为某个数目。

items.en: Coster meant to cost or be bought for a sum.
items.cn: coster 意为值多少钱、以某价购得。

items.en: English cost named the price paid for a thing.
items.cn: 英语 cost 指为某物付出的价钱。

items.en: It also names the price paid in effort, time or health.
items.cn: 它也指用精力、时间或健康付出的代价。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words in -ost or -ast, and the meaning group names other words for what is paid.
note.cn: 形近组收集以 -ost 或 -ast 结尾的短词，近义组列出其他表示所付之物的说法。

entries.definition: the money asked for a thing
the money demanded for a service

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a price tag, then move to a victory paid for in health and to a repair that empties a wallet.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一张价签开始，再到用健康换来的胜利，最后到掏空钱包的维修。

normal.en: Cost is the price tag plus everything the price tag hides.
normal.cn: cost 是价签，也是价签藏起来的一切。

normal.en: The past tense does not change: it cost, it has cost.
normal.cn: 过去式不变：it cost，it has cost。

normal.en: Cheap things often cost more in the end.
normal.cn: 便宜的东西，最后往往花费更多。

normal.en: A costly mistake is one whose price arrives later.
normal.cn: 代价惨重的错误，就是账单迟到的错误。

normal.en: Effort, time and sleep can all be costs.
normal.cn: 精力、时间和睡眠都可以是代价。

abstract.en: Picture a coin lying on one pan of a balance.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币躺在天平的一端。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt longer than the thing you bought.
abstract.cn: 想象一张比你买的东西还长的收据。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked free with a small lock on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇写着免费的门，上面挂着一把小锁。

examples.en: The repairs will cost more than we planned.
examples.cn: 这次维修的花费会超出我们的计划。

examples.en: The ticket costs a week of his wages.
examples.cn: 这张票要花掉他一周的工资。

examples.en: He won the match at the cost of his health.
examples.cn: 他赢了比赛，代价是健康。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cost 记成「扣死他」：价格一扣，钱就没了，所以是花费与代价。

root: 源自拉丁语 constare（共同立定、值某个价钱），经古法语 coster 进入英语，本指物品所值之价，后引申为一切代价。

sensesIntro.en: From money on a tag, to a loss that is not money, and at last to the act of taking money from a pocket.
sensesIntro.cn: 从价签上的钱，到不是钱的损失，最后到从口袋里拿走钱这一动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a price tag with a hidden ledger behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张价签，背后压着一本看不见的账。

branches.en: A sum of money is named before the deal.
branches.cn: 交易之前先说出一个钱数。

branches.en: Something other than money is taken away.
branches.cn: 被拿走的不是钱，而是别的东西。

branches.en: The verb makes the object reach into your pocket.
branches.cn: 动词使物品伸手进你的口袋。

branches.en: The noun and the verb name the same money from two sides.
branches.cn: 名词与动词从两侧说同一笔钱。

branches.en: To cost can mean to take away health, time or peace.
branches.cn: 花费也可以指拿走健康、时间或安宁。

intro.en: Cost is a short base word from Latin constare, to stand at a price, with many modern compounds.
intro.cn: cost 是来自拉丁语 constare（标价）的短词根词，现代又生出许多复合词。

latinIntro.en: The standing base sta- also appears in constant, stable and stand.
latinIntro.cn: 表示站立的词基 sta- 也出现在 constant、stable 与 stand 中。

items.meaning: giving good value for the money
the price paid by the seller

definition_zh: 戏服；服装；装束
definition_en: clothes worn for a play, a party or to look like someone
core_image: 万圣节南瓜斗篷一披，普通同学瞬间变成小巫师
scene: 学校艺术节要演小红帽，大家为戏服忙了一下午。Her wolf costume made everyone laugh.
sceneCN: 这里 costume 是「戏服」（第 1 个义项：演出穿的服装）；句意是她的狼戏服把大家逗乐了。

derivatives.zh: 由 costume 加 -ed 构成，义为「穿着戏服的」
同根词 custom，义为「习俗」，是 costume 的词源核心

senses.title: Special clothes for a performance or party
senses.definition: clothes worn to look like a character in a play or at a party
senses.definitionCN: 为扮演角色或在聚会时穿的衣服
senses.example: The actors changed into their animal costumes backstage.
senses.exampleCN: 演员们在后台换上了动物戏服。
senses.why: Custom means habit, and stage clothes follow the custom of the character.
senses.whyCN: custom 意为习俗，戏服遵循角色的习俗。

senses.title: The traditional dress of a place or time
senses.definition: the typical clothes of a country, group or period
senses.definitionCN: 某国、某群体或某时代的典型服装
senses.example: She wore a beautiful national costume at the culture festival.
senses.exampleCN: 她在文化节上穿了漂亮的民族服装。
senses.why: Costume also means the dress a custom hands down through years.
senses.whyCN: costume 也指习俗流传多年的服饰。

senses.title: A set of clothes worn together
senses.definition: clothes of one style worn as a set
senses.definitionCN: 风格统一的一套衣服
senses.example: His swimming costume was left at home by mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 他的泳衣被忘在了家里。
senses.why: The pieces belong together like one character's outfit.
senses.whyCN: 各件属于一套，如同一个角色的行头。

intro.en: Costume grew from the same root as custom, habits of dressing.
intro.cn: costume 与 custom 同根，都是穿着的习俗。

items.en: The Latin word consuetudo meant custom or habit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 consuetudo 意为习俗、习惯。

items.en: Italian costume meant custom, and then the customary style of dress.
items.cn: 意大利语 costume 意为习俗，进而指惯常的衣着风格。

items.en: French costume carried both custom and dress into learned writing.
items.cn: 法语 costume 兼指习俗与服饰，进入书面语。

items.en: English adopted costume in the eighteenth century for period dress.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪吸收 costume，指某时代的服装。

items.en: Theatre and parties made costume mean dress-up clothes today.
items.cn: 如今剧场与聚会让 costume 指化装服饰。

note.en: These words share the custom root or name clothes.
note.cn: 这些词共享 custom 词根或表示服装。

entries.definitionCN: 价格（拼写相近，词义无关）

definition_zh: adj. 暖和舒适的，温馨的；亲切的

definition_zh: 村舍；小屋；度假小屋
definition_en: a small house, especially in the countryside, or a small house used for holidays
core_image: 一栋石头小屋，茅草屋顶上飘着一缕细烟
scene: 雨落在茅草顶上，烟囱冒出细细一缕烟。They spent the summer in a small cottage by the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 cottage 指「乡村小屋」（第 1 个义项：乡下的小房子）；句意是他们在海边的一间小屋度过了夏天。

senses.title: A small country house
senses.definition: a small simple house, especially in the countryside
senses.definitionCN: 尤指乡下的简朴小房子
senses.example: They spent the summer in a small cottage by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边的一间小屋度过了夏天。
senses.why: Small walls and a low roof keep a country life warm.
senses.whyCN: 矮墙低顶，把乡间的生活捂得暖暖的。

senses.title: A house for holidays
senses.definition: a small house that people rent or keep for short holidays
senses.definitionCN: 人们租用或留着短期度假的小房子
senses.example: We rented a cottage in the hills for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在山里租了一间小屋住了一周。
senses.why: A holiday needs a roof smaller than the life you left behind.
senses.whyCN: 度假需要一个比原先生活更小的屋顶。

intro.en: Cottage goes back to Old English cot, a small hut, with the French ending -age added in medieval times.
intro.cn: cottage 可追溯到古英语 cot（小屋），中世纪时加上法语词尾 -age。

items.en: Cot meant a small hut or shelter.
items.cn: cot 意为小茅屋或遮蔽处。

items.en: Cotagium named a small dwelling with a little land.
items.cn: cotagium 指带一小块土地的小住所。

items.en: Cottage named the house of a country worker.
items.cn: cottage 指乡间劳动者的住房。

items.en: English cottage meant a small rural house.
items.cn: 英语 cottage 指乡间的小房子。

items.en: It now also names small houses kept for holidays.

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a stone wall and a low roof, then move to a rented holiday house in the hills.

normal.en: Cot is an old word for a small hut, and -age makes it a place.
normal.cn: cot 是表示小茅屋的古词，加 -age 就成了一个地方。

normal.en: A cottage is smaller than a house and warmer than a tent.
normal.cn: 小屋比房子小，却比帐篷暖和。

normal.en: Think of a low door, a small window and smoke from the chimney.

normal.en: A cottage garden grows flowers beside the vegetables.

abstract.cn: 想象墨绿山谷里的一扇暖窗。

abstract.en: Picture a key too small to open anything but a cottage door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小得只能开小屋门的钥匙。

sensesIntro.en: From a worker's small house in the country, to a small house rented for a few weeks.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone cottage with a low thatched roof and thin smoke.

branches.en: A country family lives close to the ground and the weather.

branches.en: A visitor borrows that small life for a short time.

definition_zh: 棉花；棉布；棉线
definition_en: the soft white fibre of a plant, the cloth made from it, or thread spun from it
core_image: 枝头绽开一团白云似的棉絮，手指一捏就散成细丝
scene: 老妇人把一团白软的纤维捻成线，一圈圈绕在木轴上。She wore a plain cotton shirt to the market.
sceneCN: 这里 cotton 指「棉布」（第 2 个义项：用棉花织成的布）；句意是她穿着朴素的棉布衬衫去市场。

senses.title: The plant fibre
senses.definition: the soft white fibre that grows around the seeds of a tall plant
senses.definitionCN: 长在高大植物种子周围的柔软白色纤维
senses.example: The fields were white with cotton.
senses.exampleCN: 田野被棉花染成一片白。
senses.why: A plant wraps its seeds in white and humans borrow that coat.
senses.whyCN: 植物给种子裹上白色外衣，人类借用了这层衣服。

senses.title: The woven cloth
senses.definition: cloth made from cotton fibre
senses.definitionCN: 用棉花纤维织成的布
senses.example: She wore a plain cotton shirt to the market.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着朴素的棉布衬衫去市场。
senses.why: Soft fibre becomes strong cloth when threads cross.
senses.whyCN: 柔软的纤维在经纬交错时变成结实的布。

senses.title: The spun thread
senses.definition: thread made by twisting cotton fibres together
senses.definitionCN: 把棉花纤维捻在一起做成的线
senses.example: The needle needs a length of cotton.
senses.exampleCN: 针上需要一段棉线。
senses.why: Twist a cloud of fibre and it becomes a line you can sew with.
senses.whyCN: 把一团纤维一捻，就成了能缝东西的线。

intro.en: Cotton comes from Arabic qutn, which passed through Italian cotone and Old French coton into English.
intro.cn: cotton 来自阿拉伯语 qutn，经意大利语 cotone 与古法语 coton 进入英语。

items.en: Qutn named the cotton plant and its fibre.
items.cn: qutn 指棉花这种植物及其纤维。

items.en: Cotone carried the word into Mediterranean trade.
items.cn: cotone 把这个词带进地中海贸易。

items.en: Coton named both the fibre and the cloth.
items.cn: coton 既指纤维，也指棉布。

items.en: English cotton first meant the imported cloth.
items.cn: 英语 cotton 最初指进口的棉布。

items.en: It now covers the plant, the fibre, the thread and the cloth.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖植株、纤维、棉线与棉布。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white boll of cotton opening on a dry stem.

branches.en: Crossed threads turn that coat into cloth.

definition_zh: 咳嗽；咳出
definition_en: to push air out of the throat with a sudden noise, or the act and sound of doing so
core_image: 一只手捂住嘴，肩膀猛地一抖，胸腔里冲出一声短促的气流
scene: 教室里很安静，后排有人捂着嘴压抑地咳了两声。He coughed softly and looked down at his book.
sceneCN: 这里 cough 指「咳嗽」（第 1 个义项：把气从喉间猛地咳出）；句意是他轻轻咳了一声，低头看自己的书。

senses.title: To push air out sharply
senses.definition: to force air out of the throat with a sudden loud noise
senses.definitionCN: 突然发出响声把气从喉间逼出
senses.example: He coughed softly and looked down at his book.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻轻咳了一声，低头看自己的书。
senses.why: The body uses a burst of air to sweep the throat clean.
senses.whyCN: 身体用一股爆发的气流把喉咙扫干净。

senses.title: The sound and the illness
senses.definition: the act or sound of coughing, or an illness that makes you cough
senses.definitionCN: 咳嗽的动作或声音，或引起咳嗽的病症
senses.example: She has a bad cough and a sore throat.
senses.exampleCN: 她咳嗽得厉害，嗓子也疼。
senses.why: One short sound can name both the act and the sickness behind it.
senses.whyCN: 一声短响，既能指动作，也能指背后的病。

senses.title: To bring something up
senses.definition: to clear something from the throat or lungs by coughing
senses.definitionCN: 通过咳嗽把喉间或肺里的东西排出
senses.example: He coughed up a bit of dust.
senses.exampleCN: 他咳出一点灰尘。
senses.why: The burst of air carries what the body wants gone.
senses.whyCN: 那股爆发的气流带走了身体想丢掉的东西。

intro.en: Cough is an imitative word: its sound echoes the noise it names, and it has been spelled many ways.
intro.cn: cough 是一个拟声词，读音模仿它所指的声音，历史上拼法变过许多次。

items.en: A word close to cohhian described noisy throat clearing.
items.cn: 接近 cohhian 的古词形容响亮地清嗓。

items.en: Coughen became the usual verb for the act.
items.cn: coughen 成为表示这一动作的常用动词。

items.en: The noun named both the sound and the sickness.
items.cn: 名词既指声音，也指病症。

items.en: The modern spelling settled while the sound stayed rough.
items.cn: 现代拼法固定下来，读音却依旧粗粝。

items.en: It now also means to force something out, as in cough up money.
items.cn: 今天它也指把东西逼出来，如 cough up money。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ough spelling, and the meaning group names other noisy throat actions.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ough 拼写，近义组列出其他喉间发声的动作。

entries.definition: a main branch of a tree
to cough in short dry bursts
to breathe with a whistling sound

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a hand over the mouth, then move to a winter illness and to dust leaving the throat.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一只手捂住嘴开始，再到一场冬季的病，最后到被咳出的灰尘。

normal.en: The spelling is rough, just like the sound it makes.
normal.cn: 这个拼法很粗粝，正像它发出的声音。

normal.en: Cough, though and rough all hide the same odd ending.
normal.cn: cough、though 与 rough 都藏着同样古怪的词尾。

normal.en: A dry cough has no reward; a chest cough brings something up.
normal.cn: 干咳没有结果，胸咳会带出东西。

normal.en: If you cough up money, you pay it unwillingly.
normal.cn: 如果说 cough up money，就是不情愿地掏钱。

normal.en: The past tense doubles nothing: coughed, coughed.
normal.cn: 过去式不双写：coughed、coughed。

abstract.en: Picture a small cloud of dust leaving a doorway.
abstract.cn: 想象一小团灰尘从门口冲出。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed hard against a mouth in a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的房间里，一只手紧紧捂住嘴。

abstract.en: Picture a chest rising once and then falling still.
abstract.cn: 想象胸腔猛地一鼓，随后又静下来。

examples.en: He coughed softly and looked down at his book.
examples.cn: 他轻轻咳了一声，低头看自己的书。

examples.en: She has a bad cough and a sore throat.
examples.cn: 她咳嗽得厉害，嗓子也疼。

examples.en: He coughed up a bit of dust.
examples.cn: 他咳出一点灰尘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cough 记成「口扶」：咳嗽时用手扶住口鼻，读音也像短促的一声。

root: 源自古英语中表示清嗓声的拟声词，经中古英语 coughen 定型，读音模仿喉间突然冲出的气流。

sensesIntro.en: From a burst of air, to the illness it signals, and at last to what that burst carries out.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一股冲出的气，到它所暗示的病症，最后到那股气带出来的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand over the mouth and a shoulder that jerks once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手捂住嘴，肩膀猛地一抖。

branches.en: The body fires one quick shot of air.
branches.cn: 身体射出一发短促的空气子弹。

branches.en: The same sound also names the sickness that repeats it.
branches.cn: 同一个声音也指让它反复出现的病。

branches.en: Whatever blocked the throat leaves with the blast.
branches.cn: 堵在喉间的东西随那股气流离开。

branches.en: The act and the illness wear one name.
branches.cn: 动作与病症共用一个名字。

branches.en: A cough both clears the way and shows what was in it.
branches.cn: 咳嗽既清出通道，也显露出里面有什么。

intro.en: Cough is a sound word that takes regular endings and forms compounds with medicine and drop.
intro.cn: cough 是拟声词，可加规则词尾，也能与 medicine、drop 组成复合词。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin root; its shape follows the noise, not a stem.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，它的形状跟随声音，而不是跟随词干。

items.example: Do not cough on the food.

sweet thick liquid for a cough

definition_zh: 委员会；理事会；地方议会；会议
definition_en: a group of people chosen to make decisions or give advice, especially for a town or organisation
core_image: 一张圆桌旁围坐着被推选出来的人，举手决定一件事
scene: 会议室里十二个人围坐一圈，举手表决是否修那条路。The city council voted to repair the old road.

pos.zh: 委员会；理事会；地方议会；会议

senses.title: A chosen decision group
senses.definition: a group of people chosen to make decisions or give advice

senses.title: A meeting for advice
senses.definition: a formal meeting held to discuss and advise on a matter
senses.definitionCN: 为讨论并议定某事而召开的正式会议

senses.exampleCN: 将军们在黎明前开了一次军事会议。

intro.en: Council comes from Latin concilium, a calling together, from com-, together, and calare, to call.
intro.cn: council 来自拉丁语 concilium（召集到一起），由 com-（一起）与 calare（呼喊、召集）构成。

items.en: Calare meant to call or summon.
items.cn: calare 意为呼喊或召集。

items.en: Concilium named a body called together for advice.
items.cn: concilium 指为商议而被召集起来的团体。

items.en: Concile meant an assembly or a meeting.
items.cn: concile 意为集会或会议。

items.en: English council named a group that advises a ruler.
items.cn: 英语 council 指为统治者出主意的团体。

items.en: It now names town bodies, committees and formal meetings.
items.cn: 今天它指市政机构、委员会与正式会议。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the easily confused council, counsel and consul, and the meaning group names other decision groups.
note.cn: 形近组收集易混的 council、counsel 与 consul，近义组列出其他决策团体。

entries.definition: an official living abroad to help citizens

entries.definition: the group that directs a company

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a round table of chosen people, then move to a town body and to generals meeting before dawn.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被推选者的圆桌开始，再到市政机构，最后到黎明前开会的将军们。

normal.en: Council hides the word call: people called together to decide.
normal.cn: council 里藏着 call：被叫到一起做决定的人。

normal.en: Council is the group; counsel is the advice it gives.

normal.en: A council sits at a round table so no seat looks highest.

normal.en: City council decides roads, housing and rubbish.

normal.en: The ending -il is quiet, but the word means loud debate.

abstract.en: Picture many hands rising in a single room.
abstract.cn: 想象许多只手在同一间屋子里举起。

abstract.en: Picture a round table worn smooth by elbows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被手肘磨得光滑的圆桌。

abstract.en: Picture a town seen from above as many doors and one table.
abstract.cn: 想象从高处看一座城，许多扇门和一张桌子。

examples.en: The city council voted to repair the old road.
examples.cn: 市议会投票决定修那条旧路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 council 记成「被 call 到一起的人」：被召集来议事的团体，就是委员会与议会。

root: 源自拉丁语 concilium（集会），由 com-（一起）与 calare（呼喊、召集）构成，本指被召集议事的人，后指委员会与地方议会。

sensesIntro.en: From a group called to advise, to the body that runs a town, and at last to the meeting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被召来出主意的团体，到管理城镇的机构，最后到会议本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: chosen people seated around one round table.
core.cn: 核心意象：被推选的人围坐在一张圆桌旁。

branches.en: A chosen group turns talk into advice.
branches.cn: 被选出的团体把谈话变成建议。

branches.en: A town body turns advice into local rules.
branches.cn: 市政机构把建议变成地方规矩。

branches.en: A meeting turns many voices into one plan.
branches.cn: 一场会议把许多声音变成一个方案。

branches.en: Both are bodies with the power to decide.
branches.cn: 两者都是握有决定权的机构。

branches.en: The body and its meeting share one name because the meeting is the body at work.
branches.cn: 机构与会议共用一个名字，因为会议就是机构在工作。

intro.en: Council rests on Latin calare, to call, with com-, together, and the noun shape -ium.

latinIntro.en: The calling base cal- also appears in calendar and clamour.
latinIntro.cn: 表示呼喊与召集的词基 cal- 也出现在 calendar 与 clamour 中。

homes owned by a local council

definition_zh: 忠告；劝告；律师
definition_en: advice given to someone, to give such advice, or a lawyer who speaks for a person in court
core_image: 一位长辈把两条路的利弊摊在桌上，让年轻人自己选
scene: 年轻人想退学，老师没有替他决定，只把利弊一条条摆出来。She counselled him to wait one more term.
sceneCN: 这里 counsel 指「劝告」（第 2 个义项：给出建议而不替人决定）；句意是她劝他再等一个学期。

pos.zh: 忠告；建议；律师；法律顾问

senses.title: Advice from someone wise
senses.definition: careful advice given to someone about what they should do
senses.definitionCN: 就某人该怎么做而给出的慎重建议
senses.example: He sought counsel from his old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他向年迈的老师寻求忠告。
senses.why: A second pair of eyes can see the road you cannot.
senses.whyCN: 多一双眼睛，就能看见你看不见的那条路。

senses.title: To advise someone
senses.definition: to give someone advice about a decision or a course of action
senses.definitionCN: 就决定或行动方案向某人提出建议
senses.example: She counselled him to wait one more term.
senses.exampleCN: 她劝他再等一个学期。
senses.why: Advice is a lamp handed over, not a hand that pushes.
senses.whyCN: 劝告是递过去的一盏灯，而不是推人的一只手。

senses.title: A lawyer in court

senses.definitionCN: 在法律案件中代表某人的律师
senses.example: The defence counsel asked for more time.
senses.exampleCN: 辩护律师请求多给一些时间。
senses.why: In court, advice must stand up and speak aloud.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上，建议必须站起来大声说话。

intro.en: Counsel comes from Latin consilium, advice or plan, from consulere, to consult or take counsel.
intro.cn: counsel 来自拉丁语 consilium（建议、计划），源自动词 consulere（商议、征询）。

items.en: Consulere meant to consult or ask for advice.
items.cn: consulere 意为商议或征询建议。

items.en: Consilium named a plan or a piece of advice.
items.cn: consilium 指计划或一条建议。

items.en: Conseil kept both the advice and the act of advising.
items.cn: conseil 既指建议，也指提建议这件事。

items.en: English counsel meant advice and the giving of it.
items.cn: 英语 counsel 指建议以及给出建议。

items.en: It also names the lawyer who gives advice in court.
items.cn: 它也表示在法庭上提供建议的律师。

note.en: The look-alike group sets council, consul and console beside counsel, and the meaning group names advice and lawyers.
note.cn: 形近组把 council、consul 与 console 放在 counsel 旁边，近义组列出建议与律师的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a lamp passed to a young hand, then move to a gentle warning and to a lawyer standing up in court.

normal.en: Council is the group; counsel is the advice it gives.

normal.en: The single l points like a lamp toward one path.

root: 源自拉丁语 consilium（建议、计划），来自 consulere（商议、征询），本指商议后给出的意见，后也指提供意见的律师。

sensesIntro.en: From a plan offered to a friend, to the act of offering it, and at last to the lawyer who offers it in court.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two paths laid on a table, with a lamp beside them.

branches.en: The noun and the verb name one act from two sides.

sensesIntro.cn: 听你说、给你建议，或替你说话的人。

core.cn: 核心意象：两把椅子、一张桌子、一本笔记

branches.en: Advice written down in a notebook.
A student across a desk.
Two lawyers conferring.
Someone paid to listen well.
A voice speaking for the accused.

intro.cn: counsellor 在 counsel 后加施动者后缀 -or，源出 consilium。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 consilium 意为建议，consulere 意为商议。

definition_zh: 顾问；辅导员；心理咨询师；（美国）律师；外交参赞
definition_en: a person who gives guidance, especially in law, education or mental health
core_image: 安静的办公室里，桌对面的人把纸巾盒往前推了推，墙上贴着课程表和一排值班姓名
scene: 开学第一周，一名新生因为选课和想家坐在指导老师对面，话没说完就红了眼眶。The counselor helped the freshman choose courses and adjust to campus life.
sceneCN: 这里 counselor 指学校里负责学业与生活指导的老师（第 4 个义项：学校辅导员）；句意：这位辅导员帮新生选课，并适应校园生活。图中可辨识物件：纸巾盒、课程表、值班表、两把椅子。

senses.title: A person who gives guidance
senses.definition: someone whose role is to advise another person
senses.definitionCN: 职责是向他人提出建议的人
senses.example: A counselor listened to the whole story before saying anything.
senses.exampleCN: 这位顾问听完整个来龙去脉才开口。
senses.why: The agent ending marks the person who does the advising, so the noun is the human counterpart of counsel as advice.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀标记做这件事的人，所以这个名词是「建议」的人形对应物。

senses.title: A lawyer in American usage
senses.definition: in American English, a lawyer who advises clients and may appear in court
senses.definitionCN: 在美式英语中，指为客户提供咨询、也可出庭的律师
senses.example: The counselor filed the motion on behalf of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 这位律师代表遗产一方提交了动议。
senses.why: Legal advice is the oldest branch of the trade, and American usage keeps the title for practising lawyers, especially in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 法律咨询是这门行业最古老的一支，美式用法把这个称谓留给执业律师，尤其在正式文书中。

senses.title: A therapist or mental health counselor
senses.titleCN: 心理咨询师；心理治疗师
senses.definition: a trained professional who helps people with emotional or psychological difficulties
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、帮助人们处理情绪或心理困难的专业人员
senses.example: She saw a counselor twice a month after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后，她每月见两次心理咨询师。
senses.why: The twentieth century widened the word from legal advice to therapeutic guidance, because both are forms of structured talk.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪把这个词从法律建议扩展到心理辅导，因为两者都是有结构的谈话。

senses.title: A school or college adviser
senses.titleCN: 学校辅导员；学业指导员
senses.definition: a staff member who guides students on courses, applications and personal problems
senses.definitionCN: 指导学生选课、申请与个人问题的教职员工
senses.example: The counselor helped the freshman choose courses and adjust to campus life.
senses.exampleCN: 这位辅导员帮新生选课，并适应校园生活。
senses.why: Schools needed someone between teacher and administrator, and the title transferred from law to education with the idea of guidance intact.
senses.whyCN: 学校需要一个介于教师与管理者之间的人，这个称谓便从法律转到教育，而「指导」这个观念原样保留。

senses.title: A camp counselor
senses.definition: a supervisor who looks after young campers and leads activities
senses.definitionCN: 照看年轻营员、带领活动的带队人员
senses.example: Each cabin of eight children shared one counselor.
senses.exampleCN: 每间住八个孩子的营房配一名辅导员。
senses.why: Supervision of the young is a form of guidance, so seasonal camps borrowed the same title for a temporary role.
senses.whyCN: 照看年轻人本身就是一种指导，所以季节性营地也用同一个称谓来指临时岗位。

senses.title: A diplomatic counselor
senses.definition: a senior officer at an embassy who handles a specialised area
senses.definitionCN: 使馆中负责某一专门领域的资深官员
senses.example: The cultural counselor arranged the exchange of students.
senses.exampleCN: 文化参赞安排了学生的互访。
senses.why: Diplomatic ranks adopted the word for an official who advises an ambassador within one field, keeping the advisory core.
senses.whyCN: 外交衔级采用这个词，指在某一领域向大使提供建议的官员，保留了「顾问」的内核。

senses.title: Counselor at law
senses.definition: a formal historical title for a licensed lawyer
senses.definitionCN: 历史上对持照律师的正式称谓
senses.example: The sign outside his office read counselor at law.
senses.exampleCN: 他办公室外的招牌上写着「执业律师」。
senses.why: The compound fixed the rank in a title, and the phrase survives on old brass plates long after ordinary speech dropped it.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合结构把身份固定成一个头衔，普通口语早已不用，它却还能在旧铜牌上见到。

senses.title: A specialist adviser in an organisation
senses.definition: an adviser attached to a body to cover one technical area, such as finance or genetics
senses.definitionCN: 受聘于某一机构、负责一个技术领域的顾问，如财务或遗传
senses.example: A genetic counselor explained the test results to the couple.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传咨询师向这对夫妇解释了检测结果。
senses.why: As knowledge specialised, organisations appointed advisers with a field label in front of the title, a pattern the word still follows.
senses.whyCN: 随着知识专门化，机构开始任命前面带领域标签的顾问，这个词至今仍循着这个模式。

intro.en: Counselor is counsel plus the agent ending -or, which comes from Latin -or. The base noun goes back to Latin consilium 'advice', and the American spelling with one l contrasts with British counsellor.
intro.cn: counselor 是 counsel 加施事后缀 -or，后者来自拉丁 -or。基础名词上溯拉丁 consilium「建议」，美式单 l 的拼法与英式 counsellor 相对。

items.en: Consilium meant advice, a plan or a body of advisers. It is the noun of consulere 'to consult', and not a form of the official title consul.
items.cn: consilium 指建议、计划或一群顾问。它是动词 consulere「咨询」的名词，而不是官职 consul 的形式。

items.en: The suffix -or marked the person who performs an action, as in doctor and victor. It gave English the shape of counselor, the one who gives the counsel.
items.cn: 后缀 -or 标记执行动作的人，如 doctor、victor。它给了英语 counselor 这个形态，即提供建议的人。

items.en: English first used counsel for the advice and for the adviser, before the agent ending was added to make the person explicit.
items.cn: 英语最初用 counsel 既指建议也指顾问，之后才加上施事后缀，把人明确标出。

items.en: Counselor was formed inside English rather than borrowed whole, which is why the British and American spellings differ: counsellor and counselor.
items.cn: counselor 是在英语内部构成的，而不是整体借入，所以英美拼写不同：counsellor 与 counselor。

items.en: Guidance work in schools and therapeutic work in clinics adopted the title during the twentieth century, widening it far beyond law.
items.cn: 二十世纪，学校的指导工作与诊所的治疗工作采用了这个称谓，使它远远超出法律领域。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for legal advisers, school advisers, therapists and camp staff, with the context deciding which role is meant.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指法律顾问、学校指导员、心理治疗师与营地带队人员，由语境决定所指的角色。

note.en: Group one separates the base word, the spelling variant and two look-alikes with other origins; group two sets the person against other helping roles.
note.cn: 第一组把基础词、拼写变体，与两个来源不同的形近词分开；第二组把这个人同其他助人角色作对照。

entries.definition: The advice itself or a legal team; counselor is always the person who gives the guidance.
entries.definitionCN: 指建议本身或一支律师团队；counselor 则始终指提供指导的人。

entries.definition: The same word spelled with double l in British English; the meaning does not change.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词在英式英语中的双 l 拼法，含义不变。

entries.definition: A member of a council or local assembly, built on council 'meeting'; it is not an adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 指议会或地方议会的成员，构词基础是 council「集会」；它不是顾问。

entries.definition: A diplomatic or Roman official; the word shares sounds with counsel but has a separate origin and no advisory sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指外交或罗马官员；读音与 counsel 相近，来源不同，也无顾问之义。

entries.definition: The activity of giving guidance; the counselor is the person who performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 指提供指导的活动；counselor 是从事这项活动的人。

entries.definition: A broad word for anyone who gives recommendations; counselor often implies training or a formal role.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指提出建议的人；counselor 常暗示受过训练或有正式职位。

entries.definition: A trained practitioner who treats mental or physical conditions; a counselor may advise without clinical treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 治疗身心问题的受训执业者；counselor 可能只提供咨询而不做临床治疗。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a legal practitioner; counselor is the American formal title for the same role.
entries.definitionCN: 法律执业者的日常说法；counselor 是同一角色的美国正式称谓。

entries.definition: A formal American term for a legal representative, also used in official titles.
entries.definitionCN: 美国指法律代理人的正式说法，也用于官方头衔。

entries.definition: An experienced person who guides another over time; a counselor usually works within a defined role or session.
entries.definitionCN: 以经验长期引导他人的人；counselor 通常在一个明确的角色或会谈框架内工作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real agent ending, the real legal sense and the real British spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的施事后缀、真实的法律义与真实的英式拼写。

normal.en: Counsel plus the agent ending -or gives the person whose job is the advising.
normal.cn: counsel 加施事后缀 -or，得到以「提建议」为职责的那个人。

normal.en: The British spelling doubles the l: counsellor, while the American keeps one.
normal.cn: 英式拼写双写 l，写作 counsellor；美式只写一个 l。

normal.en: Councilor is a council member, not an adviser: the base word is council, a meeting.
normal.cn: councilor 是议会成员，不是顾问：它的基础词是 council，即集会。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name the setting: school counselor, marriage counselor, camp counselor.
normal.cn: 固定说法点明场景：学校辅导员、婚姻咨询师、夏令营辅导员。

normal.en: In American formal writing the word still means a lawyer, as in counselor at law.
normal.cn: 在美国正式文书中，这个词仍指律师，如「执业律师」这一旧称。

abstract.en: Picture a tissue box pushed across a desk, a timetable on the wall behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一盒纸巾被推过桌面，身后墙上贴着课程表。

abstract.en: Picture a title that fits a courtroom, a classroom and a clinic without changing its shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不用改变外形就能嵌进法庭、教室与诊室的称谓。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose only tool is structured talk, given at a fixed hour each week.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人唯一的工具是有结构的谈话，每周在固定时间进行。

examples.en: The counselor asked one more question and then stayed quiet.
examples.cn: 辅导员又问了一个问题，然后安静下来。

examples.en: A camp counselor must know every child by name.
examples.cn: 夏令营辅导员必须叫得出每个孩子的名字。

examples.en: The embassy counselor handled the visa dispute.
examples.cn: 使馆参赞处理了那桩签证纠纷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「靠啥了」——心里没底就找顾问问一问「靠啥了」→ 辅导员、顾问

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the general adviser, through the American lawyer, the therapist, the school adviser, the camp supervisor, the diplomatic rank, the old title at law, and the specialist adviser inside an organisation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从泛称顾问开始，经美国律师、心理治疗师、学校辅导员、夏令营带队人、外交参赞、旧时的执业律师头衔，最后到机构内的专科顾问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk with a tissue box and a timetable, one person listening.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张放着纸巾盒与课程表的桌子，一个人在那里倾听。

branches.en: THE ROLE: the agent ending turns advice into a person whose job it is.
branches.cn: 角色：施事后缀把「建议」变成以此为职的人。

branches.en: THE LAW: the oldest field of advice supplies the American legal title.
branches.cn: 法律：最古老的咨询领域提供了美国的律师称谓。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: structured talk about feelings becomes a therapeutic profession.
branches.cn: 诊室：围绕情绪的有结构谈话，成为一门治疗职业。

branches.en: THE YOUNG: schools and camps appoint adults to guide students and campers.
branches.cn: 年轻人：学校与营地都安排成年人去指导学员与营员。

branches.en: THE FORMAL TITLES: embassies, old legal brass plates and specialised desks all keep the advisory core in a title.
branches.cn: 正式头衔：使馆、旧日的律师铜牌与专科岗位，都以头衔形式保留「顾问」的内核。

intro.en: Counselor is an English-built agent noun on a borrowed base, so its ending is the part that says 'the person'.
intro.cn: counselor 是在英语内部构成的施事名词，基础词是借来的，词尾才是表示「那个人」的部分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is consilium 'advice' from consulere 'to consult'; the Latin agent suffix -or supplies the ending, and the spelling -our marks the British form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁基础是 consilium「建议」，出自 consulere「咨询」；拉丁施事后缀 -or 提供词尾，而 -our 拼法标出英式形式。

definition_zh: 柜台；计数器；反对；反驳
definition_en: a long table where customers are served, a device that counts, or to speak or act against something
core_image: 一道长长的台面把顾客与货物分开，钱在台面上来回
scene: 售货员隔着玻璃台面递出车票，乘客把钱放进小托盘。She paid at the counter and took her ticket.
sceneCN: 这里 counter 指「柜台」（第 1 个义项：商店或车站办理业务的长台）；句意是她在柜台付了钱，拿走了车票。

senses.title: The serving table
senses.definition: a long flat table in a shop, bank or station where customers are served
senses.definitionCN: 商店、银行或车站中接待顾客的长台
senses.example: She paid at the counter and took her ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 她在柜台付了钱，拿走了车票。
senses.why: A flat board is all that stands between a wish and a price.
senses.whyCN: 一块平平的台面，就是愿望与价格之间的全部距离。

senses.title: To speak against
senses.definition: to reply to an argument or action in order to oppose it
senses.definitionCN: 为反对某论点或行动而作出回应
senses.example: She countered his claim with a single fact.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一个事实反驳了他的说法。
senses.why: A blow can be answered by a blow that lands first.
senses.whyCN: 一拳打来，可以用先落下的一拳回应。

senses.title: A counting device
senses.definition: a small device or dial that records a number
senses.definitionCN: 记录数字的小装置或刻度盘
senses.example: The counter clicked past nine hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 计数器咔哒一声越过了九百。
senses.why: A machine counts so that a hand does not have to.
senses.whyCN: 机器来数，手就不必数了。

intro.en: Counter comes from Old French comptoir, a counting desk, from conter, to count, and Latin computare, to reckon.
intro.cn: counter 来自古法语 comptoir（算账的台子），源自 conter（计数）与拉丁语 computare（计算）。

items.en: Computare meant to reckon or add up.
items.cn: computare 意为计算或合计。

items.en: Conter meant to count or tell.
items.cn: conter 意为计数或讲述。

items.en: Comptoir named the desk where money was counted.
items.cn: comptoir 指数钱的台子。

items.en: English counter first named a shop table for money.
items.cn: 英语 counter 最初指商店里处理钱款的台子。

items.en: It now also means a counting device and a verbal reply against something.
items.cn: 今天它也指计数器，以及针对某事的言语回应。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the counting base count-, and the meaning group names other words for opposing and for a sales point.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示计数的词基 count-，近义组列出其他表示反对与售货点的说法。

entries.definition: a local area with its own government
entries.definitionCN: 拥有本地政府的地方区域

entries.definition: to speak or act against something
a small enclosed place for service or display
entries.definitionCN: 用于服务或展示的小隔间

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a long serving table, then move to a verbal answer and to a small clicking device.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一张长柜台开始，再到一句口头回击，最后到咔哒作响的小装置。

normal.en: A counter was once a desk for counting money, so the table keeps the name.
normal.cn: counter 原本是数钱的台子，所以柜台沿用了这个名字。

normal.en: To counter is to put a word on the other side of the scale.
normal.cn: 反驳就是把一句话放到天平的另一边。

normal.en: Over the counter medicine needs no prescription.
normal.cn: 柜台药不需要处方。

normal.en: Count plus -er gives both a person who counts and a thing that counts.
normal.cn: count 加 -er，既可以是数数的人，也可以是计数的东西。

normal.en: Counter- at the front of a word means against, as in counterattack.
normal.cn: 词首的 counter- 表示反对，如 counterattack。

abstract.en: Picture a glass top with coins on one side and goods on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一块玻璃台面，一边是钱，一边是货。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows meeting head to head.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭头头顶头撞在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a small wheel turning one tooth at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小轮子一次转过一格。

examples.en: She paid at the counter and took her ticket.
examples.cn: 她在柜台付了钱，拿走了车票。

examples.en: She countered his claim with a single fact.
examples.cn: 她用一个事实反驳了他的说法。

examples.en: The counter clicked past nine hundred.
examples.cn: 计数器咔哒一声越过了九百。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 counter 记成 count（数）加 er：数钱数货的地方就是柜台，反过来顶回去就是反驳。

root: 源自拉丁语 computare（计算），经古法语 conter（计数）与 comptoir（算账台）进入英语，本指数钱的台子，后引申为计数器与反驳。

sensesIntro.en: From a table where money is counted, to a reply that counts against a claim, and at last to a device that counts alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 从数钱的台子，到针对某说法的回击，最后到独自计数的装置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long flat counter with goods on one side and money on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长柜台，一边是货，一边是钱。

branches.en: The counter holds the exchange between buyer and seller.
branches.cn: 柜台承载买卖双方之间的交换。

branches.en: A reply pushes back against a claim.
branches.cn: 一句回应把某个说法顶回去。

branches.en: A device keeps the total without a human hand.
branches.cn: 装置不用人手就能记住总数。

branches.en: Both are places or things where counting happens.
branches.cn: 两者都是发生计数的地方或物件。

branches.en: To counter and to count both weigh one thing against another.
branches.cn: 反驳与计数，都是把一物与另一物相衡量。

intro.en: Counter is count plus -er, giving a person, a place or a device connected with counting.
intro.cn: counter 由 count 加 -er 构成，表示与计数有关的人、场所或装置。

latinIntro.en: The prefix counter- also means against, as in counteract and counterattack.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 counter- 也表示反对，如 counteract 与 counterattack。

items.meaning: a table or device for counting

definition_zh: adj. 违反直觉的，不合常理的
definition_en: seeming wrong at first but perhaps true
core_image: 箭头指向与常识相反的一侧
scene: 数据表明多睡反而更累，这很违反直觉。The data says more sleep leaves people tired, which is counterintuitive.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：counterintuitive 指违反直觉的；句意是多睡反而更累违反直觉。

senses.title: Against intuition
senses.definition: not matching what you would expect
senses.definitionCN: 与想当然的相反
senses.example: The result is counterintuitive.
senses.exampleCN: 这个结果违反直觉。
senses.why: An arrow pointing the other way.
senses.whyCN: 指向另一边的一支箭。

senses.title: A surprising finding
senses.definition: a result that surprises experts too
senses.definitionCN: 连专家都意外的结果
senses.example: It is counterintuitive that noise helps.
senses.exampleCN: 噪声反而有用，这很出人意料。
senses.why: A quiet room that blocks learning.
senses.whyCN: 安静反而妨碍学习的房间。

senses.title: Hard to accept at first
senses.definition: difficult to believe until tested
senses.definitionCN: 未经检验难以相信
senses.example: The advice sounds counterintuitive.
senses.exampleCN: 这建议听上去不合常理。
senses.why: A remedy that seems backwards.
senses.whyCN: 看似倒着来的办法。

intro.en: Counterintuitive joins counter, against, to intuitive, from Latin intueri, to look at.
intro.cn: counterintuitive 由 counter（相反）与 intuitive（直觉的）组成，后者源出拉丁语 intueri（注视）。

items.en: Tueri means to look at or guard.
items.cn: tueri 意为注视、守护。

items.en: Intueri means to look upon.
items.cn: intueri 意为注视。

items.en: Intuitivus means by looking, by insight.
items.cn: intuitivus 意为凭观察洞见。

items.en: English intuitive meant known at once.
items.cn: 十八世纪英语 intuitive 意为当下即知。

items.en: Counter-intuitive named results that surprise.
items.cn: 二十世纪 counter-intuitive 指令人意外的结果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the counter- start; the near-meaning group names surprise.
note.cn: 形近组共享 counter- 开头；近义组都表示「出乎意料」。

normalIntro.en: Counterintuitive means the arrow points where you did not expect.
normalIntro.cn: counterintuitive 就是箭头指向你没料到的一边。

normal.en: Counter means against.
normal.cn: counter 意为相反。

normal.en: Intuitive means known by instinct.
normal.cn: intuitive 意为凭直觉便知。

normal.en: Counterintuitive goes against instinct.
normal.cn: counterintuitive 就是与直觉相反。

normal.en: More sleep bringing more tiredness is counterintuitive.
normal.cn: 多睡更累就违反直觉。

normal.en: Such results are often true.
normal.cn: 这类结果往往是真的。

abstract.en: An arrow pointing backwards.
abstract.cn: 倒着指的一支箭。

abstract.en: A quiet room that blocks learning.
abstract.cn: 越安静越学不进去的房间。

abstract.en: A remedy that looks like a mistake.
abstract.cn: 看着像犯错的办法。

examples.en: The finding is counterintuitive but solid.
examples.cn: 这个发现反直觉但很扎实。

examples.en: It seems counterintuitive to add noise.
examples.cn: 加噪声听起来不合常理。

examples.en: The advice was counterintuitive at first.
examples.cn: 这建议起初难以接受。

dict_mnemonic.text: counter（相反）+ intuitive（直觉的）→ 与直觉相反的，即违反直觉的。

root: 英语 counter（相反）+ 拉丁 intueri（注视）→ intuitive → counterintuitive

sensesIntro.en: A result that fights your first guess.
sensesIntro.cn: 与第一反应相左的结果。

definition_zh: n. 对应的人或物；副本
definition_en: a person or thing that matches another in another place
core_image: 两张一样的椅子隔着一张长桌相对
scene: 两国的贸易部长在机场见了各自的对应同行。The two trade ministers met their counterparts at the airport.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：counterpart 指对应的人；句意是两位部长会见各自的对应同行。

senses.title: A matching official
senses.definition: someone holding the same post elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 在别处担任同样职位的人
senses.example: The minister met her counterpart.
senses.exampleCN: 部长会见了对应同僚。
senses.why: Two chairs facing across a table.
senses.whyCN: 隔桌相对的两把椅子。

senses.title: A matching thing
senses.definition: a thing that plays the same role
senses.definitionCN: 起相同作用的物
senses.example: The leaf is the counterpart of a lung.
senses.exampleCN: 叶子相当于肺。
senses.why: Two shapes fitting as one.
senses.whyCN: 拼成一对的两个形状。

senses.title: A duplicate
senses.definition: an exact copy of a document
senses.definitionCN: 文件的完全副本
senses.example: Keep the counterpart in the file.
senses.exampleCN: 把副本归入档案。
senses.why: Two identical sheets.
senses.whyCN: 一模一样的两张纸。

intro.en: Counterpart joins counter, matching, to part, a portion.
intro.cn: counterpart 把 counter（相对应）与 part（部分）组合起来。

items.en: Contra means against or opposite.
items.cn: contra 意为相对、相反。

items.en: Pars means a part or portion.
items.cn: pars 意为部分。

items.en: English counterpart meant a copy of a deed.
items.cn: 十五世纪 counterpart 指契据副本。

items.en: It extended to matching persons.
items.cn: 十七世纪扩展到地位相当的人。

items.en: Diplomacy uses it for opposite numbers.
items.cn: 现代外交用它指对应职位者。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the counter- start; the near-meaning group names matching things.
note.cn: 形近组共享 counter- 开头；近义组都是相配之物。

entries.definition: Something equal in role or value.
A person with the same job elsewhere.

normalIntro.en: A counterpart is the same chair on the other side of the table.
normalIntro.cn: counterpart 就是长桌另一边那把同样的椅子。

normal.en: Counter means opposite or matching.
normal.cn: counter 意为相对、对应。

normal.en: Part means a portion.
normal.cn: part 意为部分。

normal.en: Two ministers of trade are counterparts.
normal.cn: 两位贸易部长互为对应。

normal.en: A leaf is the counterpart of a lung.

normal.en: Keep the counterpart in the file.
normal.cn: 把副本归档保存。

abstract.en: Two chairs facing across a table.
abstract.cn: 隔桌相对的两把椅子。

abstract.en: Two shapes fitting as one.
abstract.cn: 拼成一对的两个形状。

abstract.en: Two identical sheets of paper.
abstract.cn: 一模一样的两张纸。

examples.en: She met her counterpart in Paris.
examples.cn: 她在巴黎会见了对应同僚。

examples.en: The wheel is the counterpart of the foot.
examples.cn: 轮子相当于脚。

examples.en: Keep a signed counterpart on file.
examples.cn: 把签好的副本存档。

dict_mnemonic.text: counter（对应）+ part（部分）→ 对面那份相同的东西，即对应者、副本。

sensesIntro.en: The same role in another place, or the same paper again.
sensesIntro.cn: 别处的同一角色，或再一份同样的文件。

core.cn: 核心意象：长桌对面那把同样的椅子

A leaf doing a lung job.
Two identical signed sheets.
The other half of a pair.

definition_zh: adj. 适得其反的，产生相反效果的
definition_en: making things worse instead of better
core_image: 越用力推，车轮反而往反方向滚
scene: 催得越急，工人越慢，效果适得其反。Pushing harder made the workers slower, which was counterproductive.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：counterproductive 指适得其反的；句意是越催越慢，适得其反。

pos.zh: 适得其反的；白费力气的

senses.title: Producing the opposite
senses.definition: causing the reverse of the intended result
senses.definitionCN: 导致与预期相反的结果
senses.example: Shouting proved counterproductive.
senses.exampleCN: 大喊大叫适得其反。
senses.why: A push that rolls the cart back.
senses.whyCN: 一推之下反而倒退的车。

senses.title: Wasting effort
senses.definition: using effort that does no good
senses.definitionCN: 付出却毫无益处
senses.example: Long meetings are counterproductive.
senses.exampleCN: 冗长会议白费力气。
senses.why: Digging a hole and filling it again.
senses.whyCN: 挖坑再填回去。

senses.title: Harmful to the goal
senses.definition: damaging the aim it was meant to serve
senses.definitionCN: 损害原本要服务的目标
senses.example: Strict rules were counterproductive.
senses.exampleCN: 严规反而妨碍目标。
senses.why: A fence that keeps helpers out.
senses.whyCN: 把帮手挡在门外的篱笆。

intro.en: Counterproductive joins counter, against, to productive, from Latin producere, to lead forth.
intro.cn: counterproductive 由 counter（相反）与 productive（有成效的）组成，后者源出拉丁语 producere（引出）。

items.en: Ducere means to lead.
items.cn: ducere 意为引导。

items.en: Producere means to lead or bring forth.
items.cn: producere 意为引出、产生。

items.en: Productivus means able to produce.
items.cn: productivus 意为能生产的。

items.en: English productive meant fruitful.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语 productive 意为有成果的。

items.en: Counterproductive named efforts that backfire.
items.cn: 二十世纪 counterproductive 指弄巧成拙。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the counter- start; the near-meaning group names backfiring efforts.
note.cn: 形近组共享 counter- 开头；近义组都是白费或反噬的努力。

normalIntro.en: Counterproductive is pressing the accelerator while in reverse.
normalIntro.cn: counterproductive 就是挂着倒挡踩油门。

normal.en: Counter means against.
normal.cn: counter 意为相反。

normal.en: Productive means producing good results.
normal.cn: productive 意为有成效。

normal.en: Together they mean producing bad results.
normal.cn: 合起来就是产出坏结果。

normal.en: Shouting at workers slows them down.
normal.cn: 冲工人吼叫反而让他们更慢。

normal.en: A rule that blocks helpers is counterproductive.
normal.cn: 挡住帮手的规则适得其反。

abstract.en: A cart rolling backwards under a push.
abstract.cn: 一推就倒退的车。

abstract.en: A hole dug and refilled.
abstract.cn: 挖开又填回的坑。

abstract.en: A fence keeping helpers out.
abstract.cn: 把帮手挡住的篱笆。

examples.en: The strict deadline was counterproductive.
examples.cn: 严格期限反而帮了倒忙。

examples.en: Extra checks proved counterproductive.
examples.cn: 额外检查反倒添乱。

examples.en: It is counterproductive to hide the data.
examples.cn: 隐瞒数据适得其反。

definition_zh: adj. 无数的，数不清的
definition_en: too many to be counted
core_image: 仰头望天，星星多到根本数不完
scene: 夜空中的星星多到根本数不清。The night sky holds countless stars.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：countless 指数不清的；句意是夜空里有数不清的星星。

senses.title: Too many to count
senses.definition: so many that counting them is impossible
senses.definitionCN: 多到无法逐一计数
senses.example: She has read countless books.
senses.exampleCN: 她读过数不清的书。
senses.why: A sky packed with stars.
senses.whyCN: 挤满星星的天空。

senses.title: Vast in number
senses.definition: existing in a very large quantity
senses.definitionCN: 以极大量存在
senses.example: Countless people lined the street.
senses.exampleCN: 无数人排在街上。
senses.why: A river of people, not drops.
senses.whyCN: 人流成河。

senses.title: Seemingly endless
senses.definition: appearing to go on without end
senses.definitionCN: 看上去没有尽头
senses.example: He waited countless hours.
senses.exampleCN: 他等了无穷无尽的小时。
senses.why: A clock with no hands.
senses.whyCN: 没有指针的钟。

intro.en: Countless joins count, from Latin computare, to reckon, with the suffix -less, without.
intro.cn: countless 由 count（计数，源出拉丁语 computare「计算」）加后缀 -less（没有）构成。

items.en: Computare means to reckon together.
items.cn: computare 意为一起计算。

items.en: Conter meant to tell or count.
items.cn: conter 意为讲述或计数。

items.en: English count meant to tally.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语 count 意为清点。

items.en: The suffix -leas meant without.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -leas 意为没有。

items.en: Countless named things beyond number.
items.cn: 十六世纪 countless 指数不胜数。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the count- stem; the near-meaning group names endless quantity.
note.cn: 形近组共享 count- 词干；近义组都表示数量无穷。

normalIntro.en: Countless is a sky so full of stars that counting is hopeless.
normalIntro.cn: countless 就是星星多到根本数不完的夜空。

normal.en: Count means to tally numbers.
normal.cn: count 意为清点数目。

normal.en: The suffix -less means without.
normal.cn: 后缀 -less 意为没有。

normal.en: Together they mean without counting, too many.
normal.cn: 合起来就是无从计数、多不胜数。

normal.en: Stars in the night sky are countless.
normal.cn: 夜空中的星星数不清。

normal.en: Grains of sand on a beach are countless.
normal.cn: 海滩上的沙粒数不清。

abstract.en: A sky packed with stars.
abstract.cn: 挤满星星的天空。

abstract.en: A clock with no hands.
abstract.cn: 没有指针的钟。

abstract.en: Sand slipping through fingers.
abstract.cn: 从指缝漏走的沙。

examples.en: The library holds countless old maps.
examples.cn: 这座图书馆藏有无数旧地图。

examples.en: She has helped countless students.
examples.cn: 她帮助过数不清的学生。

examples.en: Countless details were left out.
examples.cn: 无数细节被省略了。

dict_mnemonic.text: count（计数）+ -less（没有）→ 没有计数，即数不清的。

root: 拉丁 computare（计算）→ 古法语 conter → 英语 count + -less（没有）

sensesIntro.en: Quantity that escapes all counting.
sensesIntro.cn: 无法计数的数量。
